column2: Then King Vaishravana showed himself to Muchukunda, and while the troops were being slain spoke these words:

Earlier kings with their priests, stronger than you, did not conduct themselves as you do here.
mahabharata:12:75.16	Then Vaishravana said to the king with his priest: I do not grant a kingdom not assigned to anyone,
nor do I take away what is assigned; know that, lord of the earth. Rule the whole earth given by me, hero."
I do not wish to enjoy a kingdom given by you, lord of the earth; I wish to enjoy a kingdom won by the strength of my arm.
Then King Vaishravana was filled with supreme wonder, seeing Muchukunda unshaken and established in kshatriya dharma.
Then King Muchukunda ruled the earth won by the strength of his arm, rightly devoted to kshatriya dharma.
Thus a king who knows Brahma and acts with Brahma first conquers the unconquered earth and gains great fame.
The Brahmana should have water always at hand, and the kshatriya weapons always; for on those two all that is in the world depends."

A king should be given to giving and to sacrifice, Bharata, devoted to fasting and austerity, and intent on protecting his subjects.
mahabharata:12:76.3	He should always protect the subjects by dharma, with exertion and without carelessness, and honour the righteous.
mahabharata:12:76.4	Dharma honoured by the king is honoured everywhere; whatever the king practises, that pleases the subjects.
mahabharata:12:76.5	He should always have the rod raised, like death to his enemies; he should strike down robbers everywhere and not forgive anyone from desire.
mahabharata:12:76.6	The dharma which the subjects practise here, well protected by the king—a fourth part of that dharma the king gains, Bharata.
mahabharata:12:76.7	What they study, what they sacrifice, what they give, what they worship—the king is a sharer of a fourth of that, protecting the subjects by dharma.
mahabharata:12:76.8	Whatever ill there is in the kingdom through the king's failing to protect the subjects—a fourth of that sin the king takes, Bharata.
mahabharata:12:76.9	Some say all of it, others that it is more, lord of the earth, for a cruel or lying person's deed; hear by what the king is freed from such a fault.
mahabharata:12:76.10	If wealth taken by thieves cannot be recovered, it should be repaid from his own treasury by one living by it, who is unable.
mahabharata:12:76.11	The property of Brahma (Brahmanas) should always be protected by all classes, and one should not stay in a country where one harms those twice-born.
mahabharata:12:76.12	When Brahmana property is protected, everything is protected; when their grace is gained, the king has done his task.
mahabharata:12:76.13	As beings live on the rain-cloud and birds on a great tree, men live on the king who accomplishes all aims.
mahabharata:12:76.14	The subjects cannot be protected by a king who is led by desire, ever of crooked mind, cruel and very greedy.
mahabharata:12:76.15	I do not seek the happiness of kingship; I do not wish for kingdom even for a moment. I like kingship for dharma, and there is no dharma here.
So enough of my kingdom where there is no dharma; I shall go to the forest, wishing to practise dharma.
There, in pure forests, with the rod laid down and senses subdued, I shall worship dharma as a sage eating roots and fruits."

I know your mind, that it is made of kindness; but great things cannot be won with pure kindness alone.
mahabharata:12:76.19	The world does not greatly honour you gentle, self-controlled, very noble, very righteous, weak-willed and full of disgust at dharma.
mahabharata:12:76.20	Look to the duties of kings fit for your father and grandfather; it is not the conduct of kings to stand as you wish to.
mahabharata:12:76.21	You, established in kindness mixed with faintheartedness, have gained the fruit of dharma born of protecting the subjects.
mahabharata:12:76.22	Pandu did not ask this blessing for you, nor did Kunti, nor this wisdom, dear one, with which you move.
mahabharata:12:76.23	Your father always spoke of valour, strength and goodness; Kunti prayed for greatness, strength and generosity for you.
mahabharata:12:76.24	Svaha and Svadha, ever both the human and the divine, and the ancestors and gods, ever pray for sons.
mahabharata:12:76.25	Giving, study, sacrifice and protecting the subjects—whether dharma or adharma, you were born to it by birth.
mahabharata:12:76.26	For those appointed to the burden at the proper time, bearing the load placed on them, even if they sink, son of Kunti, fame does not sink.
mahabharata:12:76.27	One who bears his burden restrained on every side without stumbling—success comes from the work itself, by faultless deeds and words.
mahabharata:12:76.28	No one here, whether righteous householder, king or celibate, has moved about with complete downfall.
mahabharata:12:76.29	A deed that is little but good is generous; what is done is better than what is undone, and nothing is worse than inaction.
mahabharata:12:76.30	When a man of good family who knows dharma attains supreme lordship, then, king, security and welfare are directed to prosperity.
mahabharata:12:76.31	A righteous man should gain the kingdom here and hold it on every side: one by gifts, another by strength, another by kind words.
mahabharata:12:76.32	What dharma is greater than that on which physicians born of good families, afflicted by fear of want, rest satisfied after reaching?
mahabharata:12:76.33	What is higher than this for heaven, what delight is supreme beyond this, what supreme lordship beyond this? Tell me if you think so.
mahabharata:12:76.34	On whom, well established, they find security at once; he surpasses even those who conquer heaven; I tell you this truly.
mahabharata:12:76.35	You are the delight of the Kurus; therefore, best of the Kurus, be king, win heaven, protect the good and slay the wicked.
mahabharata:12:76.36	May your friends live after you, dear one, with the good, as beings on the rain-cloud, as birds on a tree of sweet fruit.
mahabharata:12:76.37	May the people live after you, bold, brave, striking, kind, with senses subdued, affectionate and a sharer.

Those endowed with the marks of learning, seeing the tradition everywhere, are called equal to Brahma among Brahmanas, O king.
mahabharata:12:77.3	Those who are priests and teachers, established in their own works, are equal to gods among Brahmanas, O king.
mahabharata:12:77.4	Priests, household priests, ministers, envoys and instructors in wealth are equal to kshatriyas among Brahmanas, O king.
mahabharata:12:77.5	Horse-riders, elephant-riders, chariot-warriors and foot-soldiers among Brahmanas are equal to Vaishyas, O king.
mahabharata:12:77.6	Those without birth and deeds, misers, Brahmanas in name only, are equal to Shudras among Brahmanas, O king.
mahabharata:12:77.7	All who are not versed in the Veda and who have not installed the sacred fires—a righteous king should have a tax and forced labour from all of them.
mahabharata:12:77.8	Summoners, temple-priests, village priests of the stars, these are Brahmana outcasts, with the great-road traveller as the fifth.
mahabharata:12:77.9	From these a king with a depleted treasury may take tribute, except from those equal to Brahma and godlike.
mahabharata:12:77.12	In whose domain a twice-born becomes a thief, the knowers consider the offence to be the king's alone.
mahabharata:12:77.13	A thief through lack of livelihood, a Veda-knower or a graduate, O king, is to be supported by the king, so those who know dharma know.
mahabharata:12:77.14	If he does not turn from it, having been given a livelihood, scorcher of foes, then he should be banished from that country with his kinsmen.

The Vedic rule is that the king is owner of the wealth of non-Brahmanas; but of any Brahmanas who remain in wrong deeds,
mahabharata:12:78.3	Brahmanas who are in wrong deeds are not to be ignored by a king in any way—so the good recite the ancient conduct of kings.
mahabharata:12:78.4	In whose domain a twice-born becomes a thief, the knowers consider the offence, the sin, to be the king's alone.
mahabharata:12:78.5	By that deed they consider themselves as if accused; therefore all royal sages protected Brahmanas.
mahabharata:12:78.6	Here too they recite this ancient history, sung by the king of the Kekayas when seized by a Rakshasa.
mahabharata:12:78.7	A dreadful Rakshasa seized the lord of the Kekayas in the forest, a king devoted to Vedic study and of strict vows.
mahabharata:12:78.8	There is no thief in my country, no miser, no drunkard; no one who has not installed the fires and does not sacrifice: do not enter my realm.
In my domain there is no Brahmana who is unlearned, without vows, no non-soma-drinker, no one without the sacred fires: do not enter my realm.
Brahmanas honoured and given their share, gentle and truthful, abiding in their own works: do not enter my realm.
They do not beg, they give, skilled in truth and dharma, and they teach and study, sacrifice, and are not hired priests.
Kshatriyas who do not flee in battles protect Brahmanas, abiding in their own works in my realm: do not enter it.
They live by agriculture, cow-keeping and trade without deceit, careful, active, of good vows and truthful.
Relying on sharing, restraint, purity and friendliness, my Vaishyas abide in their own works: do not enter my realm.
My Shudras, without envy, serve the three classes as is proper, abiding in their own works: do not enter my realm.
I am a sharer with all, the wretched, the helpless, the aged, the weak, the sick and women: do not enter my realm.
I am the preserver of the dharmas of lineage, region and so on for all who follow them duly: do not enter my realm.
Ascetics in my domain are honoured, protected and shared with, treated with respect: do not enter my realm.
I do not eat without sharing, I do not approach another's wife, I never play independently: do not enter my realm.
There is no non-celibate beggar, no mendicant who is not celibate, no oblation without a priest: do not enter my realm.
I do not scorn the aged, physicians or ascetics; I am awake while the kingdom sleeps: do not enter my realm.
Learned in the Veda, an ascetic, knower of all dharma, lord of the whole kingdom, glorious, is my priest.
I seek the divine worlds by giving, by truth, by protecting Brahmanas, and I approach teachers by service; I have no fear of Rakshasas.
In my kingdom there is no widow, no Brahmana-in-name, no Brahmana wretched or a thief, no adulterer, no doer of sin; I have no fear of Rakshasas.
Not even a space of two fingers on my body is unpierced by weapons, fighting for dharma: do not enter my realm.
For cows, Brahmanas and sacrifice, people in my kingdom ever pray for my welfare: do not enter my realm."

Since you look to dharma alone in all conditions, therefore, Kaikeya, go to your home; I go in peace.
mahabharata:12:78.30	Those whose care is cows and Brahmanas and the subjects, Kaikeya, have no fear from Rakshasas, how much less from men.
mahabharata:12:78.31	Those who have Brahmanas in front and whose strength is Brahma's strength, whose guests and wives are dear to them, they are men who conquer heaven.
Therefore a king should protect the twice-born; for protected, they protect; their blessing is for kings, and the kingdom prospers well.
Therefore twice-born who remain in wrong deeds should be especially restrained by the king and also shared with, for the favour of the subjects.
The king who so acts toward townsfolk and country folk here, having enjoyed good things here, attains Indra's world."

One unable to live by kshatriya dharma may live by Vaishya dharma, taking to agriculture and cow-keeping, in calamity and loss of livelihood.
mahabharata:12:79.3	By selling which wares does a Brahmana, living by Vaishya dharma, not lose the worlds of heaven, bull of the Bharatas?

Liquor, salt, sesame, animals with manes, bulls, honey, meat and cooked food, Yudhishthira,
mahabharata:12:79.5	a Brahmana should avoid in all conditions; by selling these, dear one, a Brahmana goes to hell.
mahabharata:12:79.6	The goat, Fire, Varuna, the ram, the Sun, the horse, the earth, Virat, the cow, sacrifice and Soma are not to be sold in any way.
mahabharata:12:79.7	The good do not approve exchange of cooked for raw; one may exchange cooked for raw for the purpose of food, Bharata.
mahabharata:12:79.8	We shall eat the cooked; you prepare this"—thus considering, exchange is never adharma.
On this I shall tell you the ancient dharma for those engaged in dealings; hear that, Yudhishthira.
Grandsire, when all the subjects take up weapons and depart from their own dharmas, the strength of the kshatriya wanes.
If the king is not a protector in the world, what then would be the refuge? Tell me this doubt in detail."

By giving, austerity, sacrifice, non-malice and self-control, the classes headed by Brahmanas should seek their own welfare.
mahabharata:12:79.15	Those of them who have strength of the Veda, rising on every side, should increase the king's strength, as gods Mahendra's.
mahabharata:12:79.16	For a king who is waning, Brahma alone, they say, is the refuge; therefore one who knows should rise by the strength of Brahma alone.
mahabharata:12:79.17	When a victorious king establishes security in the kingdom, then the classes should return to their own works according to dharma.
mahabharata:12:79.18	When the boundaries are overstepped and mixture is made by robbers, all classes would not be at fault bearing weapons, Yudhishthira.
mahabharata:12:79.19	But if the kshatriya order everywhere becomes hostile to Brahmanas, who is the Brahmana's protector, what is the dharma, what the refuge?
mahabharata:12:79.20	By austerity, celibacy, weapon and force, without illusion or with illusion, it should then be restrained.
mahabharata:12:79.21	The kshatriya order grown excessive, especially against Brahmanas, should be restrained by Brahma alone, for the kshatriya is born of Brahma.
mahabharata:12:79.22	From water fire, from Brahmana the kshatriya, from stone iron arose; their all-pervading energy is quenched in their own wombs.
mahabharata:12:79.23	When iron cuts stone, and fire reaches water, and the kshatriya hates the Brahmana, then those three are quenched.
mahabharata:12:79.24	Therefore the unconquerable energies and forces of kshatriyas, once risen, subside in Brahma, Yudhishthira.
mahabharata:12:79.25	When Brahma's energy has become soft and kshatriya energy weak, and all classes are wicked toward Brahmanas in every way,
mahabharata:12:79.26	those who then fight, abandoning their own lives, protecting Brahmanas, dharma and themselves,
mahabharata:12:79.27	being intelligent and wrathful, become possessors of holy worlds; for the sake of Brahmanas the taking up of weapons is allowed to all.
mahabharata:12:79.28	Heroes go to the supreme state, beyond the worlds of good sacrificers, good students and ascetics, entering the fast and the fires; people know no other dharma than self-sacrifice.
mahabharata:12:79.29	Homage and blessing to those who offer their bodies, restraining the haters of Brahmanas; may we have their world; Manu called those heroes conquerors of Brahma's world, leading to heaven.
mahabharata:12:79.30	As those bathed at the close of a horse sacrifice are purified, so are evildoers and doers of good slain by weapons in battle.
mahabharata:12:79.31	Dharma and adharma both become dharma and adharma by the circumstance of place and time; place and time are such.
mahabharata:12:79.32	Friendly ones do cruel things and win the highest heaven; the righteous doing sins go to the supreme state.
mahabharata:12:79.33	A Brahmana taking up a weapon at three times is not at fault: for self-protection, in a fault of classes, and in the restraints of a fort,
mahabharata:12:79.34	when robber forces rise, for the sake of the kshatriya order, in a mixture of classes, when the classes are bewildered, if another strong one overpowers,
mahabharata:12:79.35	Brahmana, Vaishya or Shudra, best of kings, he may protect the subjects from robbers, bearing the rod by dharma.
mahabharata:12:79.36	Whether he does the task or not, whether he is restrained or not, a weapon is not to be taken up except by a kshatriya.
mahabharata:12:79.37	One who becomes the far shore for the shoreless, the boat for those without a boat, whether Shudra or another, deserves honour in every way.
mahabharata:12:79.38	One relying on whom helpless people, protected and tormented by robbers, live as they please,
mahabharata:12:79.39	him they should worship with love as their own kinsman; a doer of a great thing deserves honour, Kaurava.
mahabharata:12:79.40	What use is a bull that does not bear, what use a cow that gives no milk, what use a barren wife, what use a king who does not protect?
mahabharata:12:79.41	As a wooden elephant, as a leather deer, as a cart without a driver on the road, as barren land,
mahabharata:12:79.42	so is a Brahmana who does not study, a king who does not protect, a cloud that does not rain; all these are useless.
mahabharata:12:79.43	He who always protects the good and destroys the wicked should be made king; by him all this is upheld.

Countermeasures and the earlier conduct are prescribed for priests; first one should know the metres and the learning of the twice-born.
mahabharata:12:80.3	Those who are ever devoted to one thing, steady, not speakers of the unpleasant, friends of one another, esteemed and equal-seeing,
mahabharata:12:80.4	in whom are kindness, truth, non-violence, austerity, uprightness, non-malice, no pride, modesty, patience, self-control and peace,
mahabharata:12:80.5	modest, steady in truth, self-controlled, non-harming of beings, free of desire and aversion, endowed with the three whites,
mahabharata:12:80.6	non-violent and satisfied with knowledge—he deserves the seat of Brahma. These great priests, dear one, are all to be honoured as they are.
mahabharata:12:80.7	This saying of the Veda that is prescribed for fees, this is to be given, this is to be given," is nowhere fixed.
This scripture is not a rule regarding wealth; the dharma of calamity is not in the scripture; this is a dreadful command of the scripture and does not look to ability.
This Vedic scripture says one should sacrifice beginning with faith; what will faith do for a sacrifice accompanied by falsehood?
Fees are a limb of sacrifice, dear one, and an enhancement of the Vedas; mantras without fees do not save in any way.
Ability should be measured by a full vessel and not less; surely, dear one, the three classes should sacrifice according to rule.
The Vedic scripture says "Soma is the king of Brahmanas"; if they wish to sell him, livelihood is not to be vain; by that purchased with dharma the sacrifice is extended.
Thus is declared by dharma, by the sages who speak of dharma: a man should be of just conduct in sacrifice and soma; a man of unjust conduct is neither for another nor for himself.
The body is the sacrificial vessels—this scripture is heard; they are well produced among the great-souled Brahmanas.
The supreme scripture says it is better than the austerity-sacrifice; I shall tell you that austerity; learned one, hear that from me too.
Non-violence, truthful speech, kindness, self-control and compassion: the steady know this as austerity, not the drying up of the body.
Disregard of the Vedas, transgression of the scriptures and disorder everywhere—that is the destruction of the self.
Learn the arrangement of the ten priests, Partha, as it is: thought is the ladle, mind the ghee, and the purifier is the supreme knowledge.
All crookedness is the path of death, uprightness the path of Brahma; this much is the range of knowledge; what will chatter do?"
Of what character and conduct should the king's minister of wealth be? In what kind should a king trust, and in what kind not?

Kings, O king, have four kinds of friends: the ally for an aim, the devoted one, the natural friend and the made friend.
mahabharata:12:81.4	The righteous-souled is a fifth friend, who belongs neither to one nor to two; where dharma is, there he is, or he would be neutral.
mahabharata:12:81.5	One should not reveal to another an aim that does not please him; kings seeking victory proceed by dharma and adharma.
mahabharata:12:81.6	Of the four, the two middle are the best; the others are always to be suspected; all are always to be suspected, and one's own work to be done in sight.
mahabharata:12:81.7	A king should never be careless in guarding friends; the world scorns a careless king.
mahabharata:12:81.8	The bad becomes good, the good becomes cruel; an enemy becomes a friend, and a friend turns bad.
mahabharata:12:81.9	Who could ever trust a man of unstable mind? Therefore what is chief should be done in plain sight.
mahabharata:12:81.14	He from whose field water goes to another's field—there all his dams are not broken against his will;
mahabharata:12:81.15	so one fearing too much water wishes to break his; one who has this mark should be named an enemy.
mahabharata:12:81.16	One who is not content with prosperity and is more wretched in decline—this they call the mark of an excellent friend.
mahabharata:12:81.17	One who thinks, Without me this one would not be," in him one should place trust, as in a father.
Increasing him by one's power, one should strengthen him on every side; he who ever prevents harm in matters of dharma is such.
One who fears harm should be known as the mark of an excellent friend; those who wish him harm are known as his enemies.
One ever afraid of calamity, content only in prosperity—such a friend is called equal to oneself.
One endowed with beauty, complexion and voice, patient, without envy, of good family and conduct, may be your next.
Intelligent, mindful, skilled, kind by nature, who is never corrupted whether honoured or dishonoured,
whether priest, teacher, or an intimately praised friend, he who lives in your house as minister and is highly honoured,
he should know your supreme counsel and the nature of wealth and dharma; trust in him should be as in a father.
Neither two nor three should be employed; they would not forgive each other; from one purpose division among beings always arises.
One who is chiefly concerned with fame and stands by agreement, who does not hate the able and makes able ones,
who would not abandon dharma from desire, fear, greed or anger, skilled, of adequate speech—he may be your next.
Brave, noble, learned, skilled in understanding, of good family, endowed with conduct, patient and without envy,
such ministers should be appointed, established in all works, honoured, shared with, well assisted and well employed.
Entrusted wholly to fitting tasks, engaged in great affairs, they produce good results."
[Time said:] "Neither I, nor this Death, nor this serpent, hunter, is the cause; the creature is guilty in its death; we are not the instigators."
Vivimshati's sons, O king, were fifteen, all valiant archers, devoted to Brahmanas and truthful.
And I did not listen to Vasudeva's meaningful word: 'Let this sinful, ill-minded one be slain with his ministers.'
What kshatriya, thinking himself one, would slay sleepers as if they were dead? The Yadavas will not forgive what you did, son of Hridika.
[Vaishampayana said:] Having said this, the mighty-armed one went on without looking back, and only the dog followed him, whom I have often mentioned to you.
I am Nakula, I am Sahadeva, I am Dhrishtadyumna, and Draupadi and the sons of Draupadi—thus they cried out.
